title: Duchy of Holstein
capsule: During the First Schleswig War (1848–1851), Holstein's German-speaking nobility and the Schleswig-Holstein Provisional Government rebelled against Danish rule, backed by the Prussian army acting on a mandate from the German Confederation. Russian diplomatic pressure proved decisive: tsar Nicholas I mobilized troops and sent the Baltic Fleet to Danish waters, warning Prussia that Denmark could not be absorbed into Germany, compelling Prussia to sign the Armistice of Malmö in August 1848. The Schleswig-Holstein army was formally dissolved on 1 April 1851, and the London Protocol of May 1852 reaffirmed Danish sovereignty over Holstein while requiring it to remain constitutionally distinct from Denmark proper. Holstein remained under Danish rule until the Second Schleswig War of 1864, when Prussia and Austria defeated Denmark and forced its cession.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's territory during 1848–1853 is well-defined by the German Confederation's administrative boundaries; the disputed period's cartography is adequately attested in 19th-century sources.
